cultural.vision_reason: A carved and painted wooden kachina doll depicting a Mud Head Clown figure with case mask, protuberances, feathers, and dance costume elements — a well-documented Hopi ritual art form. This directly matches the claimed Hopi attribution.

physical.title: kachina-doll
physical.summary: Kachina-doll; carved of wood; in the form of Mud Head Clown; circle of wood for base; kachina stands on base on right foot, left foot raised behind, arms outstretched; wears case mask on head with round protruberance on either side and one on back, pointed protruberance out top decorated with feathers, eyes and mouth protrude from front; painted reddish-brown with white markings, black circle outlined in white with white dots on stomach; red felt scarf around neck; black felt skirt with green and red stripe along bottom, beige sash around waist; beige arm bands on upper arms, leg bands around ankles; lower arms and lower legs painted black with white spots; hands painted white; black wool tied around wrists and knees; holds turquoise drum with white skins from beige felt strap in left hand; "Mudhead by P.y." written on bottom.
